title: Trump Announces 'Project Freedom': US Navy to Escort Stranded Ships Through Strait of Hormuz
detail: President Trump announced 'Project Freedom' on May 3, 2026 via Truth Social — a plan to deploy US Navy assets to guide stranded commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has effectively blocked to most non-Iranian shipping since the start of the war on February 28. Approximately 2,000 vessels carrying up to 20,000 seafarers were stranded in or near the strait, with many running low on food and supplies. Trump called the operation a 'humanitarian gesture' and announced the deployment of guided-missile destroyers, over 100 aircraft, unmanned platforms, and approximately 15,000 service members — with escort operations to begin Monday May 4. The Strait of Hormuz carries roughly one-fifth of global oil and gas exports; before the conflict, over 100 ships transited daily. The IMO documented at least 19 vessel attacks since the conflict began, killing 10 seafarers and injuring 8. US national gas prices had climbed to $4.44/gallon. The announcement raised immediate concerns about confrontation with Iran, which has warned against any foreign military presence in the strait. Defense analysts noted a key constraint: fewer than a dozen US Navy vessels are specifically configured to defend commercial shipping in the confined, mine-rich Hormuz passage. Iran issued an immediate military threat (see May 4 events).

media.caption: Trump announces 'Project Freedom' — US Navy escort plan for ~2,000 stranded commercial ships blocked in the Strait of Hormuz, May 3, 2026

title: Trump Formally Notifies Congress That Iran Ceasefire Reset War Powers Resolution Clock; Democrats Reject Legal Theory
detail: The Trump administration on May 3, 2026 sent a formal notification to Congressional leaders arguing that the indefinite ceasefire in place since April 7 had reset — not merely paused — the War Powers Resolution 60-day authorization clock. The notification argued that the ceasefire constitutes a suspension of 'hostilities' within the meaning of the 1973 WPR, entitling the administration to a fresh 60-day window before Congress must authorize the conflict or demand a military withdrawal. Under the administration's legal theory, the next potential WPR deadline would fall in early July 2026. Democratic senators led by Tim Kaine immediately and forcefully rejected the argument, reiterating that it has 'no basis in the statute' — which was deliberately written to prevent technical resets via pauses. Kaine and colleagues announced they were continuing to explore litigation options. Republicans declined to publicly comment, effectively acquiescing to Trump's legal position without endorsing it. Constitutional scholars noted the ceasefire-pause theory had never been tested in any US court. The notification came as Trump simultaneously announced 'Project Freedom' — an aggressive escalation in the Hormuz standoff that could re-ignite hostilities, raising the stakes on the unresolved WPR constitutional question.

media.caption: Trump sends formal War Powers Resolution notification to Congress claiming ceasefire reset the 60-day authorization deadline; Democrats reject the legal theory, May 3, 2026

title: Washington Post-ABC-Ipsos Poll: Trump Disapproval Hits Record 62% — Highest of Second Term
detail: A Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll published May 3, 2026 found President Trump's disapproval at 62% — the highest recorded figure of his second term — with 37% approval. Multiple independent polls simultaneously confirmed the downward trend: G. Elliott Morris's polling average (FiftyPlusOne / Silver Bulletin) showed net approval at -18.8, a second-term low; Newsmax reported the result with the headline 'Trump Disapproval Hits 62%, a Two-Term High.' The pattern is consistent across methodologies: Reuters/Ipsos (34% approve), AP-NORC (33% approve), and Pew Research Center (34% approve, published May 1). Specific issue-level drivers: 64% say the Iran war is 'not worth the cost'; only 22% approve Trump's handling of cost of living; immigration approval at 41% (from 53% post-election). The sustained multi-pollster consensus around 33–37% approval is the most significant political signal of Trump's second term to date. Midterm election cycles begin in late 2026, and multiple Republican strategists cited the Iran war — particularly the Hormuz standoff and now Project Freedom — as the primary electoral liability.

media.caption: Washington Post-ABC-Ipsos poll shows Trump disapproval at 62%, a second-term record high, amid Iran war and cost-of-living frustration, May 3, 2026
